approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (A Tax Plan for the COVID-19 Economic Recovery) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would cut income tax for individuals to help the economy recover from the coronavirus pandemic.
It would bring forward planned tax threshold changes and replace the existing low income tax offset with a new one, starting from the 2020-21 income year.
The low and middle income tax offset would stay for 2020-21 but end after the 2021-22 income year.
Brings forward tax threshold changes to the 2020-21 income year.
Replaces the existing low income tax offset with a new one from 2020-21.
Extends the low and middle income tax offset for one more year.

Labor supported the five tax measures in the omnibus bill, including bringing forward stage 2 tax cuts, increasing the small business threshold to $50 million, and the temporary loss carry-back, but expressed reservations about the research and development tax incentive and temporary full expensing due to limited time to consider them.

The bill accelerates stage 2 personal income tax cuts to 1 July 2020, retains the low- and middle-income tax offset for 2020–21, and provides $17.8 billion in tax relief for 11.6 million individuals, with singles receiving up to $2,745 and dual-income families up to $5,490. It also introduces temporary loss carry back for companies with turnover up to $5 billion, expands small business tax concessions to a $50 million turnover threshold, reforms the R&D tax incentive, and allows full expensing of eligible depreciable assets for businesses with turnover under $5 billion until 30 June 2022.
Treasury Laws Amendment (A Tax Plan for the COVID-19 Economic Recovery) Act 2020
